$comment: tools/cpu-sweep.ts reads this. `calibration` is the calibration workload's cold median on the reference runner, with the digest of the workload it timed; every reading is scaled to that runner. `routes` lets a route over the 8 ms gate stay up to its own ceilingMs, with the reason it costs that much today. Each ceiling is the highest of three scaled CI runs (2026-10-09, on an EPYC 9V45, a Xeon 8573C and an EPYC 7763) plus 20%, rounded up to the half millisecond; those runs agreed within 4%. --gate fails on an entry for a route the sweep doesn't know, and prints an entry whose route now reads under 8 ms as stale, so the list only shrinks.

calibration.machine: INTEL(R) XEON(R) PLATINUM 8573C, GitHub ubuntu-latest, CI run 37871813404

/photos/query.json?q=classic+chrome+brid.why: parses the four photo JSON files (metadata, alt text, thumb hashes, semantics), prepares scoring fields for every photo and ranks them, then serializes 100; #1208 took out the ICU collator, and the next lever is scoring fields prepared at build (an owner's call)

/agent-ready.why: the sweep refuses outbound fetch, so this times the probe's error path, not a real check; not profiled yet

/photos/query.json?q=red+car.why: the same parse, prepare and ranking as the 100-result query, serializing 25

/finger.why: renders the finger terminal frame per request (it's in config/per-request-pages.json); not profiled yet

/search?q=brotli.why: search.ts prepares every record of the site index on first use and caches it per isolate, so a cold request pays the whole prepare; not profiled since #1208

/ask?query=dictionary.why: the same cold search prepare as /search
